summary.headline: R Systems Q1 CY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue rose 29.9% YoY to INR 574.8 crore; adjusted EBITDA margin 20.1%, helped by rupee depreciation.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 3.5% QoQ and 29.9% YoY to INR 574.8 crore ($62.8 million), with Novigo consolidated for a full quarter and rupee depreciation supporting the numbers. Management said organic revenue was flat QoQ, citing fewer days and Q4 fixed-price true-ups, and that Novigo's restated revenue is about $21–22 million a year after accounting alignment versus the roughly $32 million quoted at acquisition. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 115.7 crore (20.1% margin), which management said is about 19% excluding the currency benefit. Utilisation was deliberately reduced to about 80.5% (from a peak of about 84%) to build AI and data bench and COE capacity. Trailing-12-month ACV wins rose to $82.5 million from $76.5 million last quarter.

segments.name: Geography (share of revenue)
segments.commentary: Americas 69.3%, APAC 17.5%, Europe 9.6%, Middle East and Africa 3.6% (mainly Middle East, added via Novigo); broadly stable QoQ.

segments.name: Client concentration
segments.commentary: Top client 5.8% of revenue; top 3 at 11.5% (from 13.2%), top 5 at 16% (from 18.2%), top 10 at 24% (from 26.9%), reflecting a larger revenue base as top-10 dollar revenue held flat.

segments.name: Vertical (per management)
segments.commentary: TIPS (Tech, Internet, Platforms and Services) is the largest vertical at about 40% of revenue; Telecom, Media, Entertainment and Healthcare follow. Vertical split is disclosed in the Annual Report, not the quarterly release.

guidance_outlook: No formal forward guidance given; management said it expects organic and combined growth to remain on track.
Management expects EBITDA margin to be maintained in the high-teens to around 20% range, citing operational leverage, revenue mix and favourable exchange rates.
SG&A run-rate is expected to return to about USD 11 million per quarter from about USD 10 million in Q1, with sales and marketing investment continuing to rise.
Fixed-price share of revenue expected to keep rising: about 10% until 2024, about 15–16% in 2025, with no target mix set.
Novigo's Middle East exposure, hit by the regional crisis in Q1, is expected to recover and add to growth.
capex_capacity: Utilisation deliberately reduced to about 80.5% from a peak of about 84%, a 2–2.5 percentage-point dip over the last two quarters, to build AI and data COE and bench.
Over 1,400 employees are AI EV certified, out of about 5,400 total employees; attrition about 11%, below industry.
AI studio EXIQO launched, combining people with the Optima AI platform (built over about 20 months, covering 130+ projects, about 50 agents and 1,500+ prompts).
Forward cover of USD 46.25 million at an average rate of 91.13 at year-end.
Hedge accounting adopted from 1 January: INR 18 crore fair-value loss moved to hedge reserve in equity, to be reclassified to P&L later.
demand_pricing: Trailing-12-month ACV wins $82.5 million, up from $76.5 million last quarter; Q1 wins included an AI API platform for a research advisory firm, a life-insurance platform modernisation, a hyperscaler AI project and a life-sciences loyalty programme.
About 29% of revenue comes from AI and AI-enabled services (management noted this is not system-tracked).

Average deal sizes said to be rising for R Systems as end-to-end transformation deals replace feature-level work, even as AI lowers effort per deal (example: a 3-million-line legacy migration at about $1 million, versus $1.5–2 million traditionally).
Over 90% of revenue is discretionary project spend; a Novigo cross-sell pipeline includes close to a dozen joint deals and three clients receiving R Systems delivery.
Token costs for client output are borne by the client in almost all cases; R Systems bears its own token costs for training and R&D.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI in SDLC threaten growth, and how will frontier-model firms entering IT services affect R Systems?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI in SDLC expands the addressable market for a projects-based business with over 90% discretionary revenue; deal sizes per unit of work fall, but TAM expansion more than compensates. It views the frontier-lab services move as validation that AI is a people problem, and will assess competition as it develops.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Q1 growth mainly from full-quarter Novigo consolidation, and is organic growth returning from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Novigo's accounting was aligned to R Systems policies, moving some licence revenue from gross to net and changing fixed-price accounting. Restated Novigo revenue is about $21–22 million a year versus about $32 million at acquisition. Organic growth was flat QoQ, attributed to fewer days and Q4 true-ups, and management said it sees no challenge to positive outlook for Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Blackstone and Anthropic consulting venture: threat to mid-market players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees the venture as early-stage and as validation of its playbooks; Blackstone portfolio access gives a faster path to some companies, but deals are still won on merit against competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SG&A fall, and what is the normal run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop from INR 114.3 crore to INR 91.4 crore reflected reversal of a conservative AR provision after collections and year-end provision true-up, not lower investment. Normal run rate is about USD 11 million a quarter versus USD 10 million in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is organic growth and the FY outlook, and how is Novigo contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organic growth was flat in Q1, but it does not give forward guidance; it pointed to new wins and expects EBITDA margins to be sustained. Novigo cross-selling is active across close to a dozen deals.

qa_highlights.question: How are GCCs and token costs affecting the business?
qa_highlights.answer: R Systems has helped about 8–9 mid-market clients set up GCCs since launching the service about six quarters ago, which it sees as a growth lever. Token costs for client output are mostly borne by clients, and Optima AI FinOps tooling is used to meter them.

risks_watch: Organic growth was flat QoQ in Q1; management did not provide a full-year organic growth outlook.
Currency tailwind: management said EBITDA excluding rupee depreciation would be about 19%, not 20.1%.
Utilisation at about 80.5% due to AI bench investment; recovery is needed to protect margins.
Shrinking average deal sizes per unit of work from AI productivity, and competition from PE-backed AI services ventures and frontier-model firms.
Novigo revenue restatement to about $21–22 million a year, and recovery of Middle East revenue after the Q1 regional disruption.
Gross margin fell to 36.0% from 38.9% QoQ; the Q4 fixed-price true-ups did not recur.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI positioning, deal momentum and EBITDA delivery, but cautious and explanatory on the organic growth question, which management said was flat and attributed to accounting alignment, day count and Q4 true-ups.
key_quotes: We have continued to maintain our margins in a very healthy range, as we had guided in the +17% margin, kind of a range.
So, overall, I do not see any challenges to the positive outlook for this quarter as we are in Q2, and we will continue to report accordingly.
We do try and keep track of how our AI revenue is developing, with all the investments we are making, it's not exactly coming from a system, so we are not reporting it yet.

growth.why: No formal forward revenue guidance; management says organic growth is on track but organic revenue was flat QoQ and reported YoY growth is inflated by Novigo consolidation and rupee depreciation. Margin guided to hold in the high-teens to ~20% range, with utilisation deliberately cut to 80.5% to build AI bench, not for new capacity.
